Relay Administration

The Relay Operator Who Banned His Own Phone

A routine mobile check of nos.lol tripped automated rate limits; an audit of popular clients revealed a hundredfold spread in protocol economy.

By the Editorial Staff · Citing someone [s43]

When relay operator someone glanced at the ban log for nos.lol last week, an automated script had intervened with familiar severity. On the relay there is a per-IP cap, which allows 200 REQ messages every 10 seconds, they reported. The offending IP address had dispatched 283 over-cap queries through a single websocket and reconnected 75 times within an hour under a shared mobile carrier address.

Only after investigating the flagged terminal did the operator discover the culprit: Last week I banned my own phone from my own relay (nos.lol). A routine morning browse of global feeds through YakiHonne and Coracle had triggered the defensive lockout.

The incident prompted an immediate investigation into how Nostr clients manage subscription lifecycles and network requests. The resulting diagnosis showed stark disparities across the ecosystem: There is a 100x difference among client's handlings of REQs.

Database-first clients such as Damus, Amethyst, Gossip, and Nostur exhibited strict discipline, querying local stores and keeping live requests near zero during scrolling. In contrast, heavier web clients fired uncached requests per mounted card, replayed leaked pagination subscriptions on reconnects, or looped continuously when receiving CLOSED frames without backoff. The operator urged readers to favor disciplined clients to avoid triggering automated protective bans.

Encrypted Messaging

Vector Shipped Four Releases and Secures HRF Grant

Funding from the Bitcoin Development Fund backs widescreen desktop client and encrypted calls as European trilogue negotiations resume.

Dispatch · Citing V E C T O R [s500]

Vector Privacy published its third-quarter report for 2026, marking four shipped releases, 33 new features, and 49 bug fixes across its decentralized communication client. The project also confirmed a development grant from the Human Rights Foundation totaling over 500 million satoshis through the Bitcoin Development Fund.

Vector remains free and open source. There is no investor at the table, no equity sold, and no obligation attached beyond building what we already said we were building.

The grant directly finances three upcoming deliverables: Vector's maiden release on iOS, a four-pane widescreen desktop shell, and end-to-end encrypted voice and video calls scheduled for milestone v0.5.0.

Knowledge Infrastructure

From Papers to Provenance in Machine Science

As publishers expose literature to AI agents through MCP, the crisis shifts from generating hypotheses to verifying them.

Analysis · Citing WendyDing [s16], [s498]

A convergence of academic infrastructure and AI agent architectures has accelerated across the publishing world. Silverchair recently introduced its Research Bridge, packaging journal catalogs, licensing rules, and versioning metadata into Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoints that research agents can invoke directly.

Yet machine-readable access is merely half the equation. With preprint server arXiv capping individual submissions at two papers per month and model inference costs dropping precipitously, scientific production capacity faces a deluge of automated claims.

The bottleneck, WendyDing observes, is verification: Machine-readable knowledge is only the beginning. Machine-verifiable science is the harder problem. The future belongs to structured scientific records containing claims, methods, and cryptographic provenance rather than static PDFs.

Philosophical Margins

On Storing Value vs. Generating Meaning

In a widely noted passage on sovereignty and monetary tools, Kudzai Kutukwa warned against treating financial instruments as objects of veneration: It can only store value and a life spent storing value, without generating meaning, is just a more disciplined version of the fiat rat race. [s494]

True sovereignty, Kutukwa argued in the surrounding essay, requires 100 percent responsibility for one's life and the courage to build rather than mere passive balance accumulation.
